title: The Milk That Turned to Water (ML)
summary: A dishonest dairyman who watered down his milk finds his bag of coins divided by a monkey. Birbal explains the poetic justice of nature.
full_text:
A dairy merchant in the outskirts of Agra named Bhola was notorious for his cheating. Every morning, he mixed two gallons of river water into every two gallons of milk before selling it in the city. Over ten years, he accumulated a heavy leather bag filled with four hundred silver rupees.

Rejoicing in his wealth, Bhola was walking along the riverbank on a hot afternoon to buy gold ornaments in Agra. Feeling thirsty, he placed his moneybag on a rock and waded into the river to drink.

High in a sprawling banyan tree sat a curious monkey. The animal leaped down, snatched the shiny leather bag, and scrambled back to the highest bough!

Bhola screamed in horror, throwing stones and pleading with the animal: 'Drop that bag, you monkey! That is my life's savings!'

The monkey chattered playfully, untied the leather drawstring, and reached inside. Pulling out a handful of silver coins, the monkey dropped one coin onto the dry riverbank, and tossed the next coin into the deep river water! *Plop!*

The monkey repeated the process methodically: one coin to the land, one coin into the water. Two hundred silver coins fell onto the grass, and two hundred coins sank forever to the muddy riverbed!

Bhola wept bitterly, collecting his remaining two hundred coins.

Birbal, who was traveling past with his escort, listened to the merchant's lament. Birbal smiled with profound irony:

'Do not weep, Bhola. Divine justice has merely audited your books with absolute fairness!

'The two hundred coins you earned from honest milk fell safely on the dry land for you to keep. The two hundred coins you earned by selling river water have returned directly to the river! Nature has merely separated the milk from the water.'

Humbled by the lesson, the merchant repented and vowed never to dilute his milk again.
